scripts.//demo:sound: The same walkthrough with a soundtrack. Needs Xvfb, pulseaudio and ffmpeg, because a page recording cannot carry audio that the page synthesises.
scripts.//verify: Everything a change has to survive that can be checked off the filesystem. Run it before pushing.
scripts.verify: npm run lint && npm run verify:types && npm test && npm run verify:window && npm run verify:lock && npm run verify:identity && npm run verify:opening && npm run verify:budget
scripts.//verify:types: The linter does not typecheck and vitest does not either, so without this a type error reaches CI through the build and nowhere earlier.
scripts.//verify:opening: Asks the encoded film which shot each caption lands on. Imports the cue table out of src/opening.ts, so it needs the type stripping that odds.mjs needs.
scripts.//verify:live: These need something serving the game, so they are not in the chain above. verify:play and verify:audio want a dev server (npm run dev); verify:deploy wants the published URL, and fails unless the commit stamped into that page is BUILD_SHA (default: local HEAD), which is how you tell a republished preview from a cached one.
scripts.//probe:spread: Not a check. Fires one cue sixteen times and prints the distribution verify:audio reads one sample of, for when a threshold fails on one machine and passes on another.
scripts.//probe:fingerprint: Not a check either. Records the SHAPE of every sound in the mix - octave bands relative to each sound's own total, so level drops out - and diffs two recordings of it. The one question verify:audio cannot answer is 'is this the same soundtrack', because every threshold in it is a ratio between two numbers from the same run.
scripts.//odds: The engine is TypeScript and the scripts import it directly rather than keeping a second copy of the bands. Node 22.14 needs to be told to strip the types; 22.18 and up does it unasked.
